report.summary: Chunk 2 of artifacts.py: defines ResolveReport, literal resolution, schema reading (CSV/JSON/NPY), SchemaComparison, and compare_schema. Claims about determinism, bounded I/O, and schema comparison are checkable and kept.
risks: resolve_literals | medium | _candidates function not defined in chunk; if it has side effects or is non-deterministic, determinism claim could be broken. | Verify _candidates is pure and deterministic.

handoff.purpose: Defines ResolveReport, resolve_literals, schema readers (CSV/JSON/NPY), SchemaComparison, and compare_schema.

symbols.name: ResolveReport
symbols.note: Dataclass holding edges, unresolved, ambiguous, external lists. Has counts() method.

symbols.name: resolve_literals
symbols.note: Binds literals to known files. Deterministic; sorts lists. Returns ResolveReport.

symbols.name: Column
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with name, dtype, shape. Has to_dict().

symbols.name: ArtifactSchema
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for schema info. Has known property and to_dict().

symbols.name: _csv_schema
symbols.note: Internal: reads CSV/TSV header from bytes. Returns ArtifactSchema.

symbols.name: _json_schema
symbols.note: Internal: reads JSON schema from bytes. Returns ArtifactSchema.

symbols.name: _npy_schema
symbols.note: Internal: reads NPY header using struct. Returns ArtifactSchema.

symbols.name: OPTIONAL_READERS
symbols.note: Dict mapping family names to optional dependencies.

symbols.name: SCHEMA_FROM_CODE
symbols.note: Constant set to NOT_SUPPORTED; placeholder for future implementation.

symbols.note: Returns ArtifactSchema from a bounded read. Pure, no I/O.

symbols.name: SchemaComparison
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for comparing declared vs observed schema. Has agrees property and to_dict().

symbols.name: compare_schema
symbols.note: Compares ArtifactSchema against declared fields. Returns SchemaComparison.

claims.text: Deterministic; every list sorted at the end.
claims.why: The function sorts known, literals_by_file keys, and all result lists (edges, unresolved, ambiguous, external) before returning.

claims.text: A literal that names nothing in it is COUNTED, never bound to a near-match — and one that names several is counted as ambiguous, because picking the first would be a stably reproduced fabrication.
claims.why: Code: if no hits, appends to unresolved; if len(uniq)>1, appends to ambiguous. Does not pick first.

claims.text: An off-tree URL has no second node, so it is an attribute of the referring file, never an edge. Same rule as markdown.py.
claims.why: Code checks _URL.match(lit.raw) and appends to rep.external, not edges.

claims.text: True only when the schema was actually read. An empty column list on a NOT_SUPPORTED artefact is not 'no columns' — it is 'we did not look'.
claims.why: known property returns self.status == READ. NOT_SUPPORTED status would yield False.

claims.text: NPY header, parsed with struct — the format is documented and stable.
claims.why: Function uses struct.unpack to parse header, checks magic bytes and major version.

claims.text: The caller does the I/O and passes at most MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES; this keeps the module pure and testable, and keeps the read bound in one place.
claims.why: Function takes blob (bytes) and truncated flag; no I/O. Relies on MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES constant (defined elsewhere).

claims.text: missing_in_artifact is the one that bites: the code names a field the file does not have. That is the renamed-branch defect, and it survives every test suite that does not read the file.
claims.why: SchemaComparison includes missing_in_artifact field; docstring explains its significance.

claims.text: NOT comparable is a first-class answer. If the schema was never read, this returns comparable=False with the reason — it does not report every declared field as missing, which would turn 'we could not look' into a wall of false findings.
claims.why: Function checks schema.known; if false, returns SchemaComparison with comparable=False and reason.

observations.what: resolve_literals uses _candidates function which is not defined in this chunk; its determinism and behavior are unknown.
MAX_COLUMNS and MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES constants are referenced but not defined in this chunk; they are presumably defined elsewhere.
NOT_SUPPORTED and UNREADABLE constants are used but not defined in this chunk; assumed imported or defined elsewhere.
artifact_family and artifact_node_id functions are called but not defined in this chunk; their behavior is unknown.
compare_schema uses schema.rel which is the first argument to ArtifactSchema; that attribute is not explicitly defined in ArtifactSchema dataclass but is passed as 'rel' parameter.
